questions.question: Read the following statement: 'Two intersecting lines cannot be parallel to the same line'. Explore if this is an equivalent version of Euclid's Fifth Postulate and justify.
solutionSteps: This statement is known as Playfair's Axiom.
If two lines intersect, they cannot both be parallel to a third line. If they were, they would have to be parallel to each other, which contradicts that they intersect.
This is logically equivalent to the Fifth Postulate because both lead to the same geometric conclusions regarding parallel lines.

questions.question: Using Euclid's axioms and postulates, prove that every line segment has one and only one mid-point.
solutionSteps: Suppose a line segment AB has two mid-points C and D.
Then AC = 1/2 AB and AD = 1/2 AB.
This is only possible if C and D coincide. Therefore, the mid-point is unique.

questions.question: The statement 'Given two distinct points, there is a unique line that passes through them' is a fundamental assumption. Is this an axiom, a postulate, or a theorem? Justify your classification.
solutionSteps: It is a basic assumption specific to geometry.
Euclid stated it as 'To draw a straight line from any point to any point'.
It is accepted without proof, thus it is a postulate.

questions.question: Check the consistency of these two axioms: (i) If two lines intersect, vertically opposite angles are not equal. (ii) When a ray stands on a line, the sum of adjacent angles is 180°. Justify using known geometric theorems.
solutionSteps: Axiom (ii) is the familiar Linear Pair Axiom.
Using the Linear Pair Axiom, we can mathematically prove that vertically opposite angles are ALWAYS equal.
Axiom (i) contradicts this proven result. Therefore, a system containing both is inconsistent.

questions.question: Provide a rigorous definition of a 'Square'. Identify which terms in your definition would be considered 'Undefined Terms' in the Euclidean system.
questions.finalAnswer: Definition involving points, lines and angles.
solutionSteps: Definition: A square is a quadrilateral (polygon with four sides) where all sides are equal and all angles are right angles.
Undefined terms involved: Point (used for vertices), Line (used for sides).
Other terms needing definition: Angle, Equality.
